s1.syndrome_frame: Asymptomatic calcified mass on the maxilla with a hard, mineralized structure
salient_findings: calcified mass on the right anterior maxilla
mucosal fenestration with a hard, mineralized structure
discrete radiopaque lesion on periapical radiograph
key_facts: hard, mineralized structure approximately 1 cm in diameter
discrete radiopaque lesion on periapical radiograph

raw.syndrome_frame: Asymptomatic calcified mass on the maxilla with a hard, mineralized structure
salient_findings: calcified mass on the right anterior maxilla
mucosal fenestration with a hard, mineralized structure
discrete radiopaque lesion on periapical radiograph
key_facts: hard, mineralized structure approximately 1 cm in diameter
discrete radiopaque lesion on periapical radiograph

shortlist.label: Odontoma
shortlist.why_kept: Matches the description of a hard, mineralized structure and is a common cause of asymptomatic calcified masses on the jaw

shortlist.label: Maxillary exostosis
shortlist.why_kept: Initial diagnostic hypothesis and consistent with the location and description of the mass

shortlist.label: Osteoma
shortlist.why_kept: Possible cause of a discrete radiopaque lesion and a hard, mineralized structure

shortlist.label: Cemento-ossifying fibroma
shortlist.why_kept: Could explain the presence of a calcified mass with a hard, mineralized structure

shortlist.label: Focal cemento-osseous dysplasia
shortlist.why_kept: A plausible cause of an asymptomatic calcified mass on the jaw with a hard, mineralized structure

raw.rationale: The presence of a hard, mineralized structure and a discrete radiopaque lesion on the periapical radiograph, along with the location on the right anterior maxilla, supports the diagnosis of maxillary exostosis, which is a benign bony growth.

rejected.label: Odontoma
rejected.why: Odontoma is typically associated with impacted teeth and would not usually present as a solitary, asymptomatic mass on the maxilla.

rejected.label: Osteoma
rejected.why: While osteoma could present as a hard, mineralized structure, it is less common in the maxilla and the description does not specifically suggest osteoma over maxillary exostosis.

rejected.label: Cemento-ossifying fibroma
rejected.why: Cemento-ossifying fibroma tends to be larger and more aggressive than the described lesion, and often has a softer, more fibrous component.

rejected.label: Focal cemento-osseous dysplasia
rejected.why: Focal cemento-osseous dysplasia typically occurs in the posterior mandible, not the anterior maxilla, making it less likely than maxillary exostosis.
